status.question: Does a trust-region fit that uses a neural surrogate as its model, corrected at each centre with the NGSpice value and Jacobian, reach direct-NGSpice accuracy with fewer NGSpice calls? Thesis under test: neural surrogates do not rank candidate cards in the order NGSpice ranks them, and inverse networks trained on simulations have large errors on measured devices (model misspecification).

answer.text: Same search with NGSpice in place of the surrogate, 43 parameters, round 1: all-device RRMS 0.2382 → 0.1125 (combined 0.2289 → 0.1053). The pipeline value is from its final selection rerun with the same surrogate and the rule that rejects candidates with failed included curves; 18 of 18 devices are valid. Before the fix the stored pipeline value was 0.2375, with 1 failed device (0.2395 over the 17 valid devices, 0.2920 penalized).

The round-1 43-parameter surrogate orders its own picks and the direct-fit cards opposite to NGSpice on 16 of 18 devices (surrogate 0.2474 vs 0.5074; NGSpice 0.2382 vs 0.1269, all-device), with the picks from the final selection rerun with failed-curve rejection. With the picks made before the fix the count was 17 of 18 (surrogate 0.2034; NGSpice 0.2375 stored, 1 device with a failed included curve).

Six surrogate architectures in the same search, 43 parameters, round 1: end-to-end all-device RRMS 0.2274–0.2549 vs 0.1125 with NGSpice in place of the surrogate; the lowest test loss (FNO) has the highest end-to-end RRMS. Diagnostic ablation on the measured devices, not used for method selection.

Learning curves, paper MLP / DeepONet / FNO at 10,732 → 85,853 training samples: test loss 4.8–5.4× lower; end-to-end all-device 0.2588 → 0.2348, 0.2581 → 0.2274, 0.2494 → 0.2549 (combined 0.2483 → 0.2248, 0.2477 → 0.2193, 0.2397 → 0.2448); NGSpice swap 0.1125. Diagnostic ablation.
Tandem inverse network (A), seven parameters: median device RRMS 0.0258 on held-out simulated devices, 0.6344 on measured devices.
Hybrid trust-region fit: DEV results at 500–5000 calls on 36 targets are in [dev-iter1](#claim-dev-iter1).

blocks.text: Each node is a method variant registered as a DEV arm in `out/research/dev/arms.json`. Method selection uses DEV only. DEV results for n1a, n1b and n1c: [dev-iter1](#claim-dev-iter1).

items.name: n1a · sketched Jacobians
items.method: At each trust-region centre, k = 8 directional NGSpice probes (Gauss-Newton step, top singular vectors of the transported prior, one Gaussian direction) plus secant and Broyden updates replace the 43-call FD Jacobian; a full FD Jacobian at the first centre, on refresh, and on prior mismatch. Control: the same code with no surrogate.

items.name: Hermite discrepancy correction
items.method: Multi-centre gradient-enhanced (Hermite) GP correction of the surrogate-NGSpice discrepancy, first-order consistent at the centre, using every NGSpice call including rejected trials. Proposed in iteration 1 and not selected for implementation.

items.name: n1c · CMA-ES call-trace baseline
items.method: CMA-ES (sigma0 0.3, popsize 15) then bounded TRF, and lq-CMA-ES, on the same oracle, bank start, objective and call accounting as the trust-region arms, with an exact trace of best RRMS against cumulative NGSpice calls.

items.name: n1b · anytime racing
items.method: Eight zero-call surrogate presearch starts, racing of trust-region runs by predicted reduction per NGSpice call, optimistic-bound drops, surrogate-proposed restarts.

items.label: DEV
items.value: Held-out simulated targets `set_0` and `set_1` (18 devices each, 36 targets) on the full round-1 43-parameter box, through `CRYOML_TARGET_OVERRIDE`. Method development and tuning read only DEV results.

items.label: TEST
items.value: The 18 real 77 K devices, simulated `set_2`, and the GF180/IHP test truths. Each frozen method runs on TEST once.

items.label: Primary metric
items.value: All-device mean paper RRMS (frozen inclusion), pooled over targets, at fixed cumulative NGSpice budgets per target (500, 1000, 2000, 5000). Every call counts, Jacobian probes and cliff retries included. The final card is scored by one fresh NGSpice simulation.

items.label: Secondary columns
items.value: Per-set all-device mean and combined, median, geometric mean, worst target, fraction below 1e-2 and 1e-3, area under the log10 RRMS-vs-calls curve, median calls to reach 0.05 and 0.01. No device is excluded.

items.label: References

items.label: Paired tests

what: Question: how much of the paper pipeline's error at 43 parameters comes from the surrogate rather than from the search procedure?

Paper pipeline (cold, round 1): a 10k-card Latin-hypercube bank per device in the round-1 box, simulated in NGSpice; a forward surrogate (parameters → I–V) trained on it from random initialization; 8 diverse bank starts; bounded TRF least squares on the surrogate with 2-point FD (max_nfev 100, diff_step 0.02, regularization 1e-4); NGSpice validation of the top 4 endpoints, the 4 starts and the fallback.

what: Question: E1 stage 2 and I2-1 showed that a per-(family, curve tag) gain table T1 lowers the held-out RRMS after the card refit, while the E1 network M (inputs is_pmos, |Vgs|/VDD, |Vds|/VDD, log10 L, log10 W, log10 |I_sim| L/W) does not reach T1. A curve tag is a fixed terminal bias, so T1 is a function of polarity and bias only. I3-2 tests whether a smooth network of polarity and bias only, with no geometry input and no simulated-current input, matches T1 and beats the refit without a correction.

items: Corrected current: I_corr(V) = I_sim(card; V) · exp(g(x)), x = (is_pmos, |Vgs|/VDD, |Vds|/VDD), VDD = 1.85 V. The multiplication keeps the sign and zero crossings of I_sim.

g(x) = (1/5) Σ_{s=0..4} tanh(h_s(z)), z = standardized x (fold training mean and std; is_pmos kept 0/1); h_s = MLP 3-16-16-1 with tanh hidden units and a zero-initialized last layer (353 weights per member).

Training loss = (1/N_train) Σ_devices RRMS_dev(I_sim · exp(g), I_meas) + 1e-4 Σ ||W||², RRMS_dev = mean over the frozen-included curves of RMSE / mean |I_meas| on the trimmed points (paper metric). Adam lr 3e-3, 2000 full-batch steps, float64, seeds 0-4.

Held-out refit: minimize the residuals of I_bsim(card) · exp(g) against the held-out device's measured curves over the 43 card parameters (ngspice_fit.polish, trust-region least squares, max_nfev 400, 2 IRLS rounds, diff_step 0.01), starting from the device's direct43_r3_fd card; g frozen. Score: fresh NGSpice simulation of the best card times exp(g), strict paper RRMS with frozen inclusion.
Arms: C0_refit (control, same refit with g = 0); M_bias (primary); M_bias_geom (secondary, adds log10 L and log10 W: 5-16-16-1); T1_inloop (per-tag gains, not deployable, comparator).

Rule (pre-registered): CONTINUE only if R1 upper CI bound of R(M_bias, C0_refit) < 1 on REAL_DEV; R2 M_bias all-device <= T1_inloop + 0.005; R3 0 failed devices; R4 R(M_bias, C0_refit) <= 0.90 and 0 failed on GF180 or IHP tier c. STOP otherwise.

B1 and B2 are local refits from the same starting card as C0_refit; their max_nfev is scaled with the parameter count so that the TRF evaluations per IRLS round equal the base-box value of the same device.

what: Question: does a hybrid temperature law x(T) = par3_d(T) + sigma_h NN(geometry, par3 anchor residuals, T), with the per-device par3 law fitted on the O4 anchors (77/150/225/300 K) and a network shared across a densely characterised simulated population, predict the seven-parameter card at 110/190/260 K with lower NGSpice RRMS than par3 and lrn_mean when the truth law is outside the par3 family (tiers M and H), and not worse than par3 by more than a margin when the truth is inside it (tier W)?

The design addresses three E3b findings: lrn did not differ from lrn_mean on tier M; lrn lost to par3 on tier W; tier M and W were seen before the design. Tier H (piecewise-linear law with a kink plus a 5 K freeze-out step on vth0 and u0) was written in the pre-registration and not simulated before the decision run.

items: hyb network output initialised to 0, output penalty 0.01 mean(NN^2), early stopping that can return the zero-correction state; 5 members, each keeps the better of input sets geo_t and geo_t_res (addendum, before any NGSpice run of the new arms).
hyb_mean = par3 + population-mean residual per device type and temperature (no network).

CONTINUE: M1 GMR(hyb, par3) <= 0.80 with CI upper < 1; M2 CI upper of GMR(hyb, lrn_mean) < 1; M3 GMR(hyb, pt_interp) < 1; W1 CI upper of GMR(hyb, par3) on W <= 1.25; H1 CI upper of GMR(hyb, par3) on H < 1; H2 GMR(hyb, lrn_mean) < 1 and GMR(hyb, pt_interp) < 1 on H; F failed cells <= 10%.
KILL: not CONTINUE and any of GMR(hyb, par3) >= 0.95 (M), >= 1.50 (W), >= 1.00 (H). INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.

Its E3-rule output on tier H is INCONCLUSIVE (R_O4 0.145 < 0.25; reduction vs pt_interp 0.049 < 0.10). On tier W lrn has GMR 2.603 vs par3 (E3-rule output INCONCLUSIVE, as in E3b).

No hyb ensemble member returned the zero-correction state (best steps M 75-2999, W 25-375, H 50-125). Existing arms reproduce the E3b full runs on tiers M and W (max |difference| 0; O2 par3_pop 1.7e-7 on M).

caveats: Simulated devices only; training and test devices of each tier come from the same generator (no train-on-one-law, test-on-another condition).
Tier H was written by the same authors as tiers M and W, after seeing E3b; it is new to the hybrid design but not independent of the authors' assumptions about temperature laws.
The hyb inputs and output penalty were changed by the addendum after a synthetic unit test and before any NGSpice run of the new arms.
hyb has no gating at the anchor temperatures (pre-registered); its anchor-temperature error enters the card at all temperatures.
